title: IDF Strikes Rimal, Gaza City — New Hamas Military Wing Chief Mohammed Odeh Targeted, 6 Killed
detail: Israeli forces struck an apartment building in the Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City on May 26, 2026, targeting Mohammed Odeh — who had assumed command of the Hamas Qassam Brigades (Hamas's armed wing) after IDF killed his predecessor Izz al-Din al-Haddad in the same neighborhood on May 15. Prime Minister Netanyahu announced the target publicly. The strike killed Odeh, his wife, and son, plus three additional bystanders — six total killed — with over 20 wounded. Odeh had led the Qassam Brigades for only 11 days, making this the second Hamas military wing chief eliminated in less than two weeks. Defense Minister Israel Katz formally confirmed the kill on May 27. Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground documented the aftermath in the Rimal apartment block. The targeting of Odeh further dismantled the senior Hamas military command structure that had survived the 2023-2025 active combat phase of the war.

media.caption: Netanyahu announces IDF targeted Hamas military wing chief in Gaza strike — second Qassam Brigades chief eliminated in 12 days

title: IDF Strike on Tel al-Sultan Displacement Camp, Rafah — 45+ Killed, Egypt-Israel Border Incident
detail: An Israeli airstrike on the Tel al-Sultan displacement camp in Rafah on May 26, 2026 killed at least 45 people sheltering in tents, triggering one of the deadliest single-day tolls since the October 2025 ceasefire. Israel claimed the strike targeted two senior Hamas officials allegedly present in the camp area. The strike precipitated a brief but significant Egypt-Israel border confrontation: an Egyptian soldier on a border watchtower was killed after an Israeli armored vehicle crossed the Rafah boundary line in pursuit of Palestinians. The IDF confirmed 'a shooting incident occurred on the Egyptian border and is under review.' Egypt summoned the Israeli ambassador to Cairo and lodged a formal protest. Gaza's Health Ministry confirmed mass casualties with bodies brought to Rafah's field hospitals. The Tel al-Sultan strike, occurring on Eid al-Adha, drew immediate international condemnation from UNICEF, UN OCHA, and multiple EU member governments. Palestinian officials said the strike was deliberate targeting of a designated civilian displacement area. The Egypt-Israel incident represented the most serious bilateral military confrontation since the 2023 start of the war and introduced new diplomatic strain between Cairo and Jerusalem at a critical moment for reconstruction negotiations.

media.caption: Gaza health ministry: 45+ killed in Israeli strike on Tel al-Sultan displacement camp tents in Rafah; Egypt-Israel border incident follows

title: France Formally Bans National Security Minister Ben-Gvir from Entry Over Flotilla Abuse
detail: The French Foreign Ministry formally imposed an entry ban on Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir on May 26, 2026, citing his 'unacceptable actions' in posting a video of himself taunting bound and kneeling flotilla activists at Ashdod Port on May 20. The French ban made France the third NATO country after Poland (5-year ban, May 21) and Canada to formally bar Ben-Gvir, joining growing international diplomatic pressure. Earlier Italy had opened a criminal investigation on kidnapping and sexual assault allegations related to flotilla detentions, and nine Western nations had issued a joint condemnation on May 22. The French action was notable given France's historically strong relationship with Israel, and signaled European governments' willingness to take individual diplomatic steps against specific Israeli officials even where EU-level action was blocked. Ben-Gvir had previously been banned from entering both Poland and banned from entry to the UK, with the Israeli ambassador summoned by London.

media.caption: France formally bans Ben-Gvir from entry over flotilla detainee abuse video — May 26, 2026

title: IDF Completes Destruction of 11 km Hamas Tunnel Network in Beit Hanoun, Northern Gaza
detail: Israeli military engineers announced on May 26, 2026 the completion of a major operation in Beit Hanoun in northern Gaza, destroying approximately 11 kilometers of Hamas tunnel routes. The operation was part of Israel's sustained infrastructure degradation campaign aimed at preventing Hamas from using the tunnel system for troop movement, weapons storage, and command and control. The tunnels in Beit Hanoun connected to the northern Gaza network that had been used extensively during the October 2023–October 2025 combat phase. IDF engineers employed a combination of explosive charges and controlled flooding to collapse the tunnels. The operation was announced simultaneously with the Rimal strike on Hamas military chief Odeh, illustrating the multi-pronged nature of Israel's continuing military pressure despite the October 2025 ceasefire. Hamas has claimed its tunnel network extends over 500km across Gaza, though the IDF estimates it has destroyed over 300km of tunnels since October 2023.

media.caption: IDF completes destruction of 11 km Hamas tunnel network in Beit Hanoun, northern Gaza — May 26, 2026
